statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is true exactly when the whole string s is matched by the pattern p. Formally, let matches be the predicate on byte slices defined by: (a) matches(p,s) holds if len(p)=0 and len(s)=0, and for len(p)=0 and len(s)>0 it does not hold; (b) if len(p) >= 2 and p[1]='*', then with a=p[0] and q=p[2..], matches(p,s) holds iff either matches(q,s) holds, or (len(s)>0 and (a='.' or s[0]=a) and matches(p,s[1..]) holds); (c) if len(p)>0 and (len(p)=1 or p[1]!='*'), then with a=p[0], matches(p,s) holds iff len(s)>0 and (a='.' or s[0]=a) and matches(p[1..],s[1..]) holds. Then r=true iff matches(p,s) holds, and r=false iff matches(p,s) does not hold.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1 and len(s) <= 20; len(p) >= 1 and len(p) <= 20; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] is a lowercase English letter; for every i with 0 <= i < len(p), p[i] is a lowercase English letter, '.' or '*'; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(p), if p[i] = '*' then i > 0 and p[i-1] is a lowercase English letter or '.'. In particular p[0] != '*' and no two '*' are adjacent.
